title: Both Bases Flat and Dull / The Job Is in the Signs

blocks.text: Both Bases Flat and Dull / The Job Is in the Signs

AMaC MRCP PACES · R2-03 · Physical examination · PACES Station 1, respiratory examination · Skills A, B, D, E, G · 10 minutes (up to 6 minutes examining, then at least 4 minutes of examiner questions) · Guidelines: DWP Industrial Injuries Disablement Benefits: technical guidance (last updated 1 April 2026) · Related AMaC: AMaC pleural effusion and interstitial lung disease examination stations; this one tests the occupational cause and compensation advice
Mr Alan Strachan is 72 and retired. He has been breathless on slopes for two years. Please examine his respiratory system.
You may examine for up to 6 minutes. The examiners will then ask you questions.

sections.heading: 4. The Hook and the Examiner Trap

blocks.text: The Hook. Reduced expansion and dull bases on both sides in a man of 72 point to asbestos. Plaques, thickening and mesothelioma are separated by what they do to the chest and how they behave.

The Examiner Trap. Candidates say "bilateral effusions" or "fibrosis" and never ask about work. Pass: diffuse pleural thickening, ask about asbestos exposure, and advise on benefits. Fail: pleural effusions and nothing about his job.

rows: Think
Say
Do
Both bases are affected, so compare each with the other and with the upper zones.
"May I examine your chest? Does anything hurt? Is this angle comfortable?"
Clean hands; introduce, consent; sit him at 45 degrees; hands, face, chest wall shape; expansion at the bases, both sides.
Dull but not stony, expansion low, no crackles: that separates thickening from effusion and fibrosis.
"I'm going to tap and listen on both sides from the back. Please say 'ninety-nine'."
Percussion note; breath sounds; vocal resonance; look for a chest wall mass or biopsy scar; nodes; cover him; clean hands.
Say the sign pattern, then ask about his work, because the cause is occupational.
"Reduced expansion with dull bases on both sides suggests diffuse pleural thickening. May I ask what work he did?"
Present in order; diagnosis; occupational history; investigations; benefits advice; thank him.

R1
G
Welfare
Starts without consent; asks him to breathe hard repeatedly with no pause; leaves him exposed.
Cleans hands, introduces self, consents, asks about pain, sits him at 45 degrees, covers him afterwards.
Also offers a chaperone, allows rests between deep breaths, and keeps exposure to the minimum.
R2
A
Systematic technique
Examines the front only, or omits the hands, nodes or chest wall.
Hands, face, nodes, chest wall, then expansion, percussion and auscultation from the back, comparing sides.
Also feels the chest wall for a mass or biopsy scar and checks the legs.
R3
B
Identifying signs
Reports crackles, a stony dull note or a mass that is not present.
Finds reduced expansion at both bases, a mildly dull note and quiet breath sounds at both bases.
Also states no clubbing, crackles, chest wall mass or nodes, and a central trachea.
R4
D
Differential diagnosis
Calls it bilateral pleural effusions or pulmonary fibrosis.
Bilateral diffuse pleural thickening, most likely from asbestos.
Also separates plaques (no symptoms or signs), thickening (restriction) and mesothelioma (usually one side, pain, weight loss, effusion).
R5
E
History and investigations
Asks for no occupational history; chest X-ray only.
Asks about work, such as shipyards, lagging or insulation, and requests chest CT and spirometry.
Also says a new effusion, a growing one-sided thickening, or pain and weight loss needs urgent specialist review and biopsy.
R6
E
Benefits and safety-netting
Gives no advice on benefits; reassures without a safety net.
Advises him that he can claim Industrial Injuries Disablement Benefit if the exposure was in employed work, to seek legal advice, and to report chest pain or weight loss.

Also names diffuse pleural thickening as a prescribed disease (D9) and diffuse mesothelioma as a separate prescribed disease (D3), says self-employed work does not qualify, and advises stopping smoking.

blocks.text: High-performance is an AMaC teaching label, not an official grade. It shows what lifts a pass from adequate to convincing.
Not used for this station type.

Findings, released as each step is done: thin, mildly breathless on speaking; respiratory rate 18; pulse 76 regular; blood pressure 138/82; SpO2 94% on air; temperature 36.6 °C. Hands: no clubbing, no tar staining. Face: normal. Chest wall: no scars, no mass; symmetrical shape. Trachea central. Expansion reduced at both bases; percussion mildly dull, not stony, at both bases; breath sounds quiet at both bases; no crackles, wheeze or rub; upper zones normal. No nodes. No leg oedema.

Question ladder: 1. What do you see? (B) Reduced expansion, dull quiet bases both sides. 2. Cause? (D) Diffuse pleural thickening. 3. What would you ask him? (E) Work history. Told: pipe lagger in a shipyard. 4. How is thickening different from plaques and mesothelioma? (D) 5. What would you advise? (E) Benefits, legal advice, safety net.

Curveballs: He has lost 4 kg and has night pain on one side: suspect mesothelioma, urgent specialist review. Still smokes: advise stopping. Which scan? CT chest. He was self-employed: Industrial Injuries Disablement Benefit covers employed work only, so ask about earlier employed exposure and advise legal advice.
Cleans hands, introduces self, gains consent and offers rests between breaths (G)
Inspects hands and chest wall, then compares both sides from the back (A)
Finds reduced expansion and mildly dull quiet bases on both sides (B)
States no clubbing, crackles or chest wall mass (B)
Names diffuse pleural thickening, most likely from asbestos (D)
Separates plaques, thickening and mesothelioma (D)
Asks for the occupational history and requests chest CT and spirometry (E)
Advises Industrial Injuries Disablement Benefit and legal advice (E)
Gives the safety net: chest pain, weight loss, new breathlessness (E)
Covers him, cleans hands and thanks him (G)
Fail performance
CANDIDATE: Sit back. [R1 Fail]
CANDIDATE: (Percusses the front only.) [R2 Fail] There are crackles at both bases and a stony dull note. [R3 Fail] Bilateral pleural effusions. [R4 Fail]
EXAMINER: Plan?
CANDIDATE: Chest X-ray. [R5 Fail] He can carry on as normal. [R6 Fail]
Examiner note: No consent, front only, signs invented, effusions named, no work history, no advice or safety net.
Pass performance
CANDIDATE: (Cleans hands.) Mr Strachan, I'm one of the doctors. May I examine your chest? I'll sit you at 45 degrees. Does anything hurt? Is this angle comfortable? [R1 Pass]
CANDIDATE: (Hands, face, nodes, chest wall; expansion, percussion and auscultation from the back, comparing sides.) [R2 Pass]
CANDIDATE: Expansion is reduced at both bases, with a mildly dull note and quiet breath sounds. [R3 Pass]
CANDIDATE: (Covers him, cleans hands.) Thank you. [R1 Pass]
EXAMINER: Diagnosis?
CANDIDATE: Bilateral diffuse pleural thickening, most likely from asbestos. [R4 Pass]
EXAMINER: Next steps?
CANDIDATE: I'd ask about his work, such as shipyards, lagging or insulation, and request chest CT and spirometry. [R5 Pass]
EXAMINER: What would you advise him?
CANDIDATE: If he was an employee when exposed, he can claim Industrial Injuries Disablement Benefit. He should also seek legal advice and report chest pain or weight loss promptly. [R6 Pass]
Examiner note: Safe and complete. Did not separate plaques from mesothelioma or name the prescribed disease.
High-performance performance
CANDIDATE: (Cleans hands.) Mr Strachan, may I examine your chest? Would you like a chaperone? You can rest between deep breaths, and I'll keep you covered. [R1 High]
CANDIDATE: (Hands, face, nodes, chest wall for a mass; both sides from the back; legs.) [R2 High]
CANDIDATE: Central trachea, reduced expansion and mildly dull quiet bases on both sides. No clubbing, crackles, chest wall mass or nodes. [R3 High]
CANDIDATE: (Covers him, cleans hands, thanks him.) [R1 High]
EXAMINER: Diagnosis?
CANDIDATE: Diffuse pleural thickening from asbestos. Plaques cause no symptoms or signs; mesothelioma is usually one-sided with pain, weight loss and effusion. [R4 High]
EXAMINER: Next steps?
CANDIDATE: Work history, chest CT and spirometry. A new effusion, growing one-sided thickening, pain or weight loss needs urgent specialist review and biopsy. [R5 High]
EXAMINER: What would you advise him?

CANDIDATE: Industrial Injuries Disablement Benefit for employed work only, where diffuse pleural thickening is prescribed disease D9 (diffuse mesothelioma is D3, if that is diagnosed); legal advice; stop smoking; report pain or weight loss. [R6 High]
Examiner note: Added the chaperone and rests, the chest wall check, the three-way comparison, the urgent triggers and the prescribed disease number.
R4: Naming bilateral effusions. A stony dull note would fit; this mildly dull note with low expansion points to thickening, and the occupational cause is never reached.
R5: Not asking about work. The cause of the signs sits in the history, and without it the benefits advice cannot follow.
R6: Sending him away with no advice on benefits. He may have a right to a claim, and the candidate appears to stop at the diagnosis.
"Let me compare the two bases again before I go on."
"May I ask what work he did? That would settle the cause."
"May I summarise what I found and give my diagnosis?"

Diffuse pleural thickening: reduced expansion, dull and quiet bases, usually both sides, with breathlessness from restriction. Plaques alone cause no signs. Mesothelioma is usually one-sided, with pain, weight loss and effusion.

Diffuse pleural thickening is prescribed disease D9 for Industrial Injuries Disablement Benefit; diffuse mesothelioma is a separate prescribed disease, D3 (DWP technical guidance). Industrial Injuries Disablement Benefit cannot be claimed for self-employed work (GOV.UK).
THINK: Both bases flat and dull: asbestos.
SAY: "Bilateral diffuse pleural thickening; may I ask about his work?"
DO: Compare both sides; feel the chest wall.
NUMBERS: Prescribed disease D9 (DWP, April 2026).
TRAP: Calling it bilateral effusions.
FINISH: CT and spirometry; benefits; report pain or weight loss.
